description.narrative:
Oxfam in Uganda will promote Climate Smart Agriculture (CSA) as a response to climate change through local partnerships among womenand youth in Karamoja. CSA is recognized as an approach that brings together practices, technologies, services, policies and institutions that are not necessarily new but are used in the context of climate change to support farmers at various levels adapt and/or mitigate to the effects of climate change on agricultural production.
Pertinent to the success of the CSA approach is the adoption of good farming and land management practices by farmers such as basic agronomic practices, soil and water conservation, sustainableland management, and water resources management. Doing so requires attention not just to the productivity and income of rural Ugandans dependent on crop, livestock and fisheries production, but also demands explicit attention to issues of social equity.
For thatreason, Oxfam is proposing this project aiming to implement a sustainable and localized solution to building resilient livelihoods in Karamoja Sub region in the Districts of Moroto, Nakapiripirit and Amudat while putting gender at the centre through a strong focus on empowering women and youth.
Oxfam defines resilience as ‘the ability of women, men, and children to realise their rights and improve their well-being despite shocks, stresses, and uncertainty;’ through enhancement of absorptive, adaptive and transformative capacities. Our aim is to achieve longer-term and sustainable community resilience by having engaged local actors2 (e.g. local government, civil society and community-based organizations) collectively identify and implement solutions to addressing shocks and stresses as well as the causes of hazards and vulnerability with clear gender considerations.
The project will develop innovative ways ofworking with men and women using household methodologies like the Gender Action Learning System (GALS) as a way of giving people more control and reducing gender inequalities propelled by drastic climatic changes. Oxfam and its partners have already gained a wealth of experience in using the GALS methodology in projects that address value chains, gender-based violence, food security, advocacy, and village saving and lending associations. This experience indicated that the methodology could be an effective tool for making climate change interventions more gender responsive and geared towards building the resilience of smallholder farmers for improved livelihoods.
To further leverageimpact and ensure its sustainability, Oxfam’s approach will include a governance component, with policy analysis, advocacy, and capacity-building efforts focused on the linkages between agriculture and climate change. This is where women will be empoweredto participate in decision-making processes, especially on issues that affect them.
The project aims to combat food insecurity among 150 vulnerable households in the Kotido district of the Karamoja sub-region in Uganda by enhancing climate-resilient food production, improving access to agricultural inputs, and strengthening income-generating activities. It seeks to increase household income, reduce negative coping strategies, and promote sustainable livelihoods through climate-smart agriculture, value chain development, and cash-for-work interventions. The initiative prioritizes gender equity and intra-household dynamics by integrating the Gender Action Learning System (GALS) to address inequalities in resource control and decision-making. By implementing best

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Novib is one of the 17 national affiliates of the Oxfam International Confederation. It started life in 1956 as the Netherlands Organisation for International Assistance (Novib), and joined forces with Oxfam in 1994. Working together in confederation, the Oxfam affiliates can speak with one clear and compelling voice on issues of global concern: climate change, health and education forall, agriculture, trade, and conflicts and emergencies. Oxfam established this country office to support local organizations and projects. Through this local office Oxfam Novib directly contributes towards this project’s implementation.
